chunks: With this chain of narration, from Al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Jubayr al-Azrami, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

One who recites Surah 'Hashtaa' (Surah Al-Insan) in the morning of every Thursday, Allah will marry him to eight hundred virgin Hoor al-Ayn, and four thousand previously married women, and one more Hoor al-Ayn, and he will be in the company of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.الْحُورِ الْعِينِ: Hoor al-Ayn, celestial virgins in Paradise.
key_terms.ثَيِّبٍ: Previously married women, a specific category of companions mentioned in the reward.
key_terms.عَذْرَاءَ: Virgins, specifically referring to the Hoor al-Ayn in this context.
key_terms.غَدَاةِ خَمِيسٍ: The morning of Thursday, a specific time for this recommended act.
key_terms.مَعَ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ و: In the company of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), indicating high spiritual status.
key_terms.هَلْ أَتَى عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ: Surah Al-Insan (Chapter 76 of the Quran), often referred to by its opening verse.

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Insan on Thursday mornings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith emphasizes the specific virtue of reciting Surah Al-Insan on Thursday mornings, promising a unique reward of marriage to 800 virgins and 4,000 other companions. This specific enumeration reflects the Shia tradition of detailed eschatological rewards, linking the recitation to the honor of being in the company of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The emphasis on Thursday aligns with its significance as the day of Eid al-Fitr and the preparation for Friday prayers in Shia jurisprudence.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam  Muhammad  Baqir  (a.s.)  said,  “One  who  recites Surah Insan in the morning of every Thursday Allah would marry   him   to   eight   hundred   virgin   women   and   four thousand  women  who  had  been  married  previously  and give him one more Hoorul Ein and company of Muhammad (s.a.w.s.).”
